questions.question: Who is the recipient of the first-ever 'Lifetime Disturbing the Peace Award' ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salman Rushdie**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Salman Rushdie** is the recipient of the first-ever 'Lifetime Disturbing the Peace Award'.
 
• This award is presented by the **PEN America**, an organization that stands at the intersection of literature and human rights.
 
• Rushdie has been a prominent figure in defending the right to freedom of expression, particularly through his literary works.
 
• His novel, **"The Satanic Verses"**, led to significant controversy and a fatwa issued against him, highlighting the challenges faced by writers in speaking freely.
 
• The award recognizes individuals who have shown a lifelong commitment to the principles of free speech and expression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PEN America** is an organization that works to protect writers and advance literature and human rights.
 
• Salman Rushdie was born on **June 19, 1947**, in Mumbai, India.
 
• He is a British-American novelist and essayist of Indian descent.
 
• His notable works include **"Midnight's Children"**, which won the Booker Prize in 1981, and **"The Satanic Verses"**.
 
• Rushdie's writings often blend historical fiction with magical realism, addressing themes of migration, religion, and identity.

questions.question: Which prestigious award was Serena Williams honored with in 2025 for her achievements in sports and advocacy?

options.text: BBC Sports Personality of the Year
Princess of Asturias Award for Sports

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Princess of Asturias Award for Sports.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Serena Williams was awarded the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports 2025, one of Spain’s most prestigious honors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Williams is recognized as one of the greatest tennis players, with 73 career singles titles including 23 Grand Slams.**
 
• **The award recognizes her excellence in sports and advocacy for gender equality and equal opportunities.**
 
• **The prize includes €50,000 and is part of Spain’s annual awards celebrating excellence in various fields.**
 
• **The awards ceremony takes place in Oviedo and is presided over by Spain’s Princess Leonor.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Princess of Asturias Award:**__ Annual Spanish award recognizing outstanding achievements in sports, arts, literature, science, and more.
 
• __**Serena Williams:**__ Former American tennis player celebrated for her multiple Grand Slam wins and contributions to sports equality.
 
• __**Advocacy for Equality:**__ Williams is known for championing gender equality and equal opportunities in sport and society.
 
• __**Previous Recipients:**__ Includes Lindsey Vonn, IOC Refugee Olympic Team, and the New Zealand rugby team.

questions.question: What was Nikki Giovanni best known for, and what notable award did she receive in 2024?

options.text: Her works in children's literature and receiving the Nobel Prize in Literature
Her contributions to science fiction, receiving the Booker Prize for her collection of poems
Her academic work and publishing textbooks, receiving the Pulitzer Prize for poetry
Her activism and poetry on civil rights, receiving an Emmy for Exceptional Merit in Documentary Filmmaking

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Her activism and poetry on civil rights, receiving an Emmy for Exceptional Merit in Documentary Filmmaking**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Nikki Giovanni, acclaimed poet and icon of the Black Arts Movement, passed away peacefully on December 9, 2024, at the age of 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Nikki Giovanni was a renowned poet, author, and activist, known for her powerful poems on civil rights, race, and gender.
 
• She received an Emmy in 2024 for Exceptional Merit in Documentary Filmmaking for the documentary *Going to Mars: The Nikki Giovanni Project*.
 
• Giovanni published numerous volumes of poetry, essays, and more than 10 children's books, making significant contributions to literature and activism.
 
• She was a long-time faculty member at Virginia Tech, where she was Emerita Professor in the Department of English since 1987.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Nikki Giovanni was born on June 7, 1943, in Knoxville, Tennessee, and became a key figure in the Black Arts Movement.
 
• Her work addressed pressing social issues, particularly focusing on race and gender inequality.
 
• Giovanni’s latest poetry book, *The Last Book*, is scheduled for release in fall 2025.
 
• She is survived by her lifelong partner Virginia Fowler, her son and granddaughter, and several extended family members.
 
• Her death on December 9, 2024, marked the loss of a legendary figure whose impact on literature and civil rights will be remembered for generations.

questions.question: Which Pulitzer Prize category recognized the book "No Right to an Honest Living" by Jacqueline Jones?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**History**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• **BOOKS, DRAMA & MUSIC (History) - **No Right to an Honest Living: The Struggles of Boston’s Black Workers in the Civil War Era, by Jacqueline Jones (Basic Books).

 
 
• A breathtakingly original reconstruction of free Black life in Boston that profoundly reshapes our understanding of the city’s abolitionist legacy and the challenging reality for its Black residents.
 
 
 
• BOOKS, DRAMA & MUSIC (Music) - Adagio (For Wadada Leo Smith), by Tyshawn Sorey.
 
 
• Premiered on March 16, 2023 at Atlanta Symphony Hall, an introspective saxophone concerto with a wide range of textures presented in a slow tempo, a beautiful homage that’s quietly intense, treasuring intimacy rather than spectacle.
 
 
 
• BOOKS, DRAMA & MUSIC (Poetry) - Tripas: Poems, by Brandon Som (Georgia Review Books).
 
 
• A collection that deeply engages with the complexities of the poet’s dual Mexican and Chinese heritage, highlighting the dignity of his family’s working lives, creating community rather than conflict.
 
 
 
• BOOKS, DRAMA & MUSIC (General Non-Fiction) - A Day in the Life of Abed Salama: Anatomy of a Jerusalem Tragedy, by Nathan Thrall (Metropolitan Books).
 
 
• A finely reported and intimate account of life under Israeli occupation of the West Bank, told through a portrait of a Palestinian father whose five-year-old son dies in a fiery school bus crash when Israeli and Palestinian rescue teams are delayed by security regulations.
 
 
 
• The Pulitzer Prize is regarded as the highest national honor in print journalism, literary achievement, and musical composition.
 
• Established in 1917 from funds endowed by journalist and newspaper publisher Joseph Pulitzer, prizes are awarded yearly.

questions.question: Which organization received the Subhash Chandra Bose Aapda Prabandhan Puraskar for 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**INCOIS**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)** has been honored with the Subhash Chandra Bose Aapda Prabandhan Puraskar for 2025.
 
• INCOIS runs the **Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre**, recognized by UNESCO for its excellence in tsunami monitoring and alert dissemination.
 
• Its advisories significantly aided in disaster response during **Cyclone Phailin (2013)** and **Cyclone Hudhud (2014)**.
 
• Technologies like **SARAT** support the Indian Coast Guard in search and rescue missions, and **SynOPS** integrates real-time oceanic data to bolster disaster management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose Aapda Prabandhan Puraskar**: India’s prestigious award honoring outstanding contributions in the field of disaster management.
 
• **INCOIS**: Functions under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, providing essential ocean-based information, early warnings, and advisories for natural disasters.
 
• **Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre**: A UNESCO-certified system offering real-time monitoring to protect coastal populations from tsunamis.
 
• **SARAT and SynOPS**: Advanced tools enhancing search and rescue operations, as well as real-time data integration for robust disaster response.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **INCOIS Achievements**__

 __
 
• Developed early warning solutions to safeguard lives and property in coastal regions.
 
• Internationally recognized for tsunami warning capabilities, particularly after the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Award**__
 
 
• Named after Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, reflecting courage and dedication to public service.
 
• Awards individuals and organizations demonstrating exemplary work in disaster risk reduction and management.

questions.question: Who received the Sahitya Akademi Award 2024 for the book “Ek Hor ashwathama”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shri Chaman Arora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shri Chaman Arora** received the prestigious Sahitya Akademi Award 2024 for his Dogri short story collection titled **“Ek Hor Ashwathama”**.
 
• The award was announced in February 2024 and will be presented to a member of Arora's family at a ceremony in New Delhi on March 8th, 2024.
 
• This award includes a **tamrapatra** (copper plate) and a cash prize of **one lakh rupees**, according to the announcement from NEWS ON AIR.
 
• Chaman Arora’s work, written in Dogri, highlights the richness of the language and explores deep social issues through the lens of storytelling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award:**

 
 
• The Sahitya Akademi Award is one of the most prestigious literary awards in India, presented annually by the Sahitya Akademi, the National Academy of Letters, to authors of outstanding works in one of the 24 major Indian languages.
 
• It is awarded for books of exceptional literary merit in the fields of fiction, poetry, drama, and other literary genres.
 
• 
 
Established in 1954 by the Sahitya Akademi (India’s National Academy of Letters).

 
 
• 
 
Aims to recognize and promote outstanding literary work in the 22 scheduled languages of India, including English and Rajasthani.

 
 
 
 
• **Dogri Literature:**
 
 
• Dogri is a language spoken in the Jammu region of India and is known for its rich cultural and literary traditions.
 
• Shri Chaman Arora's contribution to Dogri literature through his award-winning short stories highlights the significance of regional languages in India's diverse literary landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jagadguru Rambhadracharya and Gulzar were honored with the 58th Jnanpith Award for their significant contributions to Indian literature.**

 __

questions.question: Who was awarded the 2025 Abel Prize?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Masaki Kashiwara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Japanese mathematician Masaki Kashiwara awarded the Abel Prize 2025.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• 
 
**Recipient of the 2025 Abel Prize**: Masaki Kashiwara, a Japanese mathematician.

 
 
• 
 
**Field of Contribution**:

 
 
• 
 
Algebraic analysis

 
 
• 
 
Representation theory

 
 
• 
 
Development of D-modules

 
 
• 
 
Discovery of crystal bases.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**About the Abel Prize**:

 
 
• 
 
Named after Niels Henrik Abel, a legendary Norwegian mathematician.

 
 
• 
 
Established by the Norwegian Parliament in 2002 to commemorate Abel's 200th birth anniversary.

 
 
• 
 
First awarded in 2003.

 
 
• 
 
Often regarded as the Nobel Prize equivalent in mathematics.

 
 
• 
 
Awarded by a committee in consultation with the International Mathematical Union (IMU) and the European Mathematical Society (EMS).

 
 
• 
 
Includes a cash award and a glass plaque designed by Norwegian artist Henrik Haugan.
